hunks.summary: The header says runtime-telemetry/v2 supersedes this version and points at Known Defects; the Primary consumer note is reflowed. A pointer to this contract's successor; it changes no v1 obligation.

The canonicalisation sentence becomes an explicit byte contract: UTF-8 with literal non-ASCII, sorted keys, RFC 8259 escaping, the integer bound and the non-integer numeric zone, with values outside it refused. A tightened producer rule. Restored out of v1; runtime-telemetry/v2 carries it.

A transport failure never ends a producer: it must not terminate, abandon its export loop or discard a retained batch, and only a recorded terminal refusal stops export. New producer obligations. Restored out of v1; runtime-telemetry/v2 carries it.

The canonical body and HMAC golden fixture, which implementations must reproduce byte for byte, with the Known Defects note that followed it. The fixture is a new conformance requirement, restored out of v1; runtime-telemetry/v2 carries it. The Known Defects note is kept as its own erratum hunk.

A boundary statement: ori-gateway does not produce, consume, proxy or define this contract, and SDK use does not place the endpoint inside the gateway authority boundary. Restored out of v1; runtime-telemetry/v2 carries it.

Known Defects: a note naming five points this version leaves unstated, which a producer and a receiver can settle differently and so discard readings between them, and saying runtime-telemetry/v2 resolves them. It rules on none of them and changes no obligation.

notes: Main delivers the same request bytes under runtime-telemetry/v2 delivery rules.
